decisions.decision: Keep the current block-text Canva payload model instead of redesigning schema/editor flow.
decisions.rationale: Main-branch code already uses block fields like morning_block, day1_block, and menu_day2_block, which fits the current repo state better than reverting to per-slot fields.

decisions.decision: Prioritize wiring saved fieldMapping into runtime Canva generation.
decisions.rationale: Admin already stores template field mappings, but generation appears to send canonical payload keys directly; this is the most likely reason real output may not match the user's Canva templates and sample images.

decisions.rationale: User explicitly asked to continue these three outputs, reuse the existing 1-day mapping logic, ask questions first, and align final output with the two provided 2-day sample images.

context_notes: This session did not modify repo code. It only clarified scope, explored the existing Canva/review flow, and produced an approved implementation direction. Important repo reality discovered during planning: current main branch already uses a block-based schema in src/lib/canva/field-map.ts and src/lib/canva/payload.ts, and explicit ONE_DAY/TWO_DAY support already exists across payload builders, review editors, and review actions. The likely missing last-mile integration is applying stored fieldMapping at generation time. Also note the broader working tree already had many unrelated uncommitted changes before pause-work started, so resume carefully and avoid assuming a clean tree. Grep found placeholder/TBD markers in various planning docs, but no new phase-04 summary regression was introduced by this session.
